neighbours.label: A word naming the useful role something plays ('source of energy', 'crucial habitats', 'covered expenses', 'good for'), where a complement saying what it serves comes next; plain descriptions of the same things stay quiet.
fire: Fat is a major source of energy for long runs.
Wetlands are vital habitats for migrating birds.
Eligible costs may include tools and training.
Zinc is good for a healthy immune system.
Sugar is the main source of fuel in the brain.
Hedgerows are important habitats for small mammals.
Reimbursable expenses may include hotel stays.
Oats are good for lowering cholesterol.
quiet: Fat is a soft substance found in long sausages.
Wetlands are flat and wet in early spring.
The invoice may arrive with tools and training.
Zinc is a grey metal in the periodic table.
Sugar is the main export from the island.
Hedgerows are trimmed by small tractors.
The hotel may close for a week in June.
Oats are sold in bags at the corner store.

notes: The output direction promotes ' in' across languages. Probes: ' habitats' 0.76, ' energy' 0.69, ' good' 0.42; 'common goal' read only 0.01 and 'beneficial' 0.19, so the boundary is rough.
